newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl tells parliament he confident euro coming.
newsitem.headline: Kohl tells parliament he confident euro coming.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Friday he was confident that the single European currency would be launched on schedule in 1999 and warned sceptics that there would be dark consequences if the project failed.

Speaking to parliament after the European Union and Group of Seven summits, Kohl said the euro would stimulate the economy and secure jobs. He said delaying the economic and monetary union (EMU) could spell its doom.

"To abandon EMU would mean Europe was giving up on its great challenge at a decisive moment," Kohl said. "That would bring all the negative consequences for exports, investment and jobs in Germany and harm Europe's integration. We would all pay dearly for the failure of the euro."

Kohl said the Amsterdam Treaty signed earlier in June had advanced the European Union's integration on several fronts. Job creation was a top priority at the summit along with increasing cooperation on crime fighting and a common foreign policy.
The chancellor said the "clear signal" from the Amsterdam summit was that the euro was now inevitable. He told deputies on four occasions "the euro is coming" in his 45-minute address.
"I am certain that we will introduce the euro according to plan -- punctually on January 1, 1999 and fully in line with the Maastricht criteria," he said.
